tests: [accessibility.test] Accessibility filtering children of leaf nodes root option should support the interestingOnly option
reason: Puppeteer's `interestingOnly: false` returns every node of the accessibility tree, including the generic and inline-text nodes a snapshot leaves out. Strider's snapshot has no option to keep roleless nodes, and `Snapshot.Options` has only `sources`, `depth` and `interactiveOnly`. The interestingOnly:true half of the last test is expressible and is the only part Strider has

tests: [accessibility.test] Accessibility iframes should not include iframe data if not requested
reason: Puppeteer's `includeIframes` (off by default) leaves a frame's tree out of the snapshot. Strider stitches every frame's tree in under its iframe, and `Snapshot.Options` has no switch for it, so the default this test checks has no Strider counterpart
The test's point is the node's `roledescription` (aria-roledescription, which Chromium reports only where it's valid). Strider's snapshot node carries no roledescription, so there's nothing to check
The test's point is the node's `orientation` (aria-orientation). Strider's snapshot node carries no orientation
The test's point is the node's `autocomplete` (aria-autocomplete). Strider's snapshot node carries no autocomplete
The test's point is the node's `multiselectable` (aria-multiselectable). Strider's snapshot node carries no multiselectable
The test's point is the node's `keyshortcuts` (aria-keyshortcuts). Strider's snapshot node carries no keyshortcuts

tests: [accessibility.test] Accessibility filtering children of leaf nodes elementHandle() should get the parent ElementHandle from a text node accessibility node
[accessibility.test] Accessibility filtering children of leaf nodes elementHandle() should get the shadow host ElementHandle from a text node in a shadow root
reason: Puppeteer's `elementHandle()` on a text node's accessibility node gives the element that holds the text. Strider's text nodes carry no ref, so a snapshot item can't be turned into a locator for its parent, and the shadow-host case fails the same way

tests: [accessibility.test] Accessibility should capture new accessibility properties and not prune them
reason: The test's point is that the accessibility properties of a node (busy, live, atomic, relevant, modal, roledescription, aria-invalid, errormessage, details, description) are reported and kept. Strider's snapshot node carries none of them, and its `invalid` state comes from native validation only
